entrypoints.summary: A committed ClusterFuzz-minimized XLS file is the concrete parser input for this case.
The OSS-Fuzz build recipe creates a POIHSSFFuzzer corpus from spreadsheet XLS files.

affected_components.role: Derives shared-formula range dimensions and allocates the FormulaRecordAggregate array.
Enforces the allocation bound added by the remediation.

code_slices.fixed: The constructor stores the product in allocateSize, checks it against MAX_NUMBER_AGGS through IOUtils.safelyAllocateCheck, then allocates using allocateSize.
code_slices.surrounding_context: MAX_NUMBER_AGGS is 10,000; the patch states callers can overrule the byte-array maximum through IOUtils configuration.
code_slices.vulnerable: width and height from SharedFormulaRecord endpoints were multiplied directly in the FormulaRecordAggregate array expression.

capabilities.concept: control shared-formula range area used for allocation

relation_candidates.dst: control shared-formula range area used for allocation
relation_candidates.rationale: The patch identifies malformed spreadsheets as the trigger and calculates the allocation size from shared-formula row and column range dimensions.
The pre-fix constructor multiplies width by height and uses the result as the array length.
relation_candidates.src: control shared-formula range area used for allocation

relation_candidates.rationale: The maintainer describes a malformed spreadsheet triggering a very large allocation, and the case record reports the constructor-led Security exception.
The patch inserts safelyAllocateCheck(allocateSize, MAX_NUMBER_AGGS) before constructing the array.

impact.affected_asset: Memory/resources of the process parsing the workbook.
impact.attacker_capability: Supply a malformed XLS file to an Apache POI HSSF parsing path.
impact.security_effect: Malformed XLS parsing can reach a documented very-large-allocation condition and a recorded Security exception.

causal_trace.summary: A malformed spreadsheet is documented by the maintainer patch as capable of triggering the condition; the same change commits a minimized XLS testcase.

SharedFormulaGroup derives width and height from SharedFormulaRecord row and column endpoints, multiplies them into allocateSize, and previously used that derived area without an aggregate-count limit before array initialization.
The pre-remediation operation allocates a FormulaRecordAggregate array whose length is width * height; the patch describes this as a potentially very large allocation.

The OSS-Fuzz record reports a Security exception with a crash state headed by SharedFormulaGroup initialization. The available evidence establishes an excessive-allocation condition, not a measured resource outcome or exploitation beyond parsing the malformed file.

failure.operation: new FormulaRecordAggregate[allocateSize] after allocateSize = width * height

primary_invariant.statement: The number of FormulaRecordAggregate elements initialized for a shared-formula group must not exceed the configured maximum before creating the array.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The derived range area width * height directly determined the array length before a maximum-size check.

raw_refs.role: OSS-Fuzz case record and affected/fixed ranges

quality.review_notes: The patch directly supports the range-area allocation and 10,000-element guard, while the OSV record supplies only a short Security-exception crash state. Exact malformed BIFF field values, actual allocation size, full stack/sanitizer output, and observed fixed execution are absent. Test exclusions in the patch are not treated as a passing regression result or as proof that the new guard is the observed exception.

remediation.invariant_restored: allocateSize is checked with IOUtils.safelyAllocateCheck against MAX_NUMBER_AGGS (10,000) before the FormulaRecordAggregate array is created.

state_context.attacker_state_setup: Provide the committed malformed XLS testcase or another malformed spreadsheet that reaches shared-formula group construction.
data_structure_invariants: A shared-formula range area must be bounded before allocating its FormulaRecordAggregate backing array.

numeric_domains.attacker_constraints: Computed as width * height from shared-formula record endpoint differences; concrete field values and product for the testcase are not exposed.
numeric_domains.name: allocateSize

state_context.state_machine: Workbook parsing constructs SharedValueManager and then SharedFormulaGroup for shared-formula records.
